title: Constant product function
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $I$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, and let $B=(b_a)_{a\in I}$ be a real basis of functions on $\Omega$ whose distinguished basis function is constantly $1$. For every natural number $n$ and every $x\in\Omega^n$, the product function indexed by the tuple that uses the distinguished index at every coordinate has value $1$ at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty index set $I$ with decidable equality
A real basis of functions on $\Omega$
The distinguished basis vector is constantly $1$
